Vacancy: PhD candidate The Department of Neurology of Erasmus MC has a vacancy for a PhD candidate: Research on outcome measures for patients with neuralgia, for 36 hours per week. Job content Guillain-Barré syndrome (GBS) and chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy (CIDP) are two serious forms of nerve inflammation. Patients with this condition develop severe symptoms and neurological deficit. GBS and CIDP are partially treatable but the response to treatment is often insufficient. The research you will be part of focuses on developing and validating a specific set of patient-reported outcome measures and other outcome measures for these diseases in order to measure and improve the effect of treatment and care. Work environment The study will be conducted at Erasmus MC in close cooperation with the Kenniscentrum Meetinstrumenten (Kmin, Amsterdam UMC). Erasmus MC is the national expertise centre for the care and research of GBS and CIDP. Here, a multidisciplinary team of experts works diligently to develop better care for these patients. The Kmin is an internationally renowned research group for the development of patient-reported outcome measures. Profile You have completed the course in Medicine, Health Sciences, Psychology or a similar degree. Experience in scientific research is an advantage but not essential. You have scientific interest in this project and the ambition to obtain a PhD. You are a team player with very good social skills. You have an eye for detail, you are strong analytically. You have a good command of the English language, both written and spoken. Check the terms and conditions for employment at Erasmus MC. What we offer A challenging position within the largest University Medical Centre (UMC) in the Netherlands with high ambitions in the areas of care, education and research. Working with an enthusiastic group of medical and measurement experts. A temporary contract for the duration...

CWI logo  Postdoc/researcher (m/f/x) Centrum Wiskunde & Informatica (CWI) has a vacancy in the QuSoft research group for a talented Postdoc/researcher (m/f/x)on the subject of characterisation, learning and testing in bosonic quantum computers.  Job description Theoretical models of quantum computers typically consist of qubits. Physics, however, naturally provides us with other natural modalities of quantum computing. First among these is bosonic quantum computing, which has seen substantial experimental progress, but comparatively little work on the theoretical computer science side. The goal of this postdoc position is to perform research on property testing, learning theory and characterisation of bosonic quantum systems, as well as the classical simulation of bosonic quantum computation. This position is established as part of the Quantera consortium Batir-le-chat, which brings together researchers from the Netherlands, Germany and France to work on the theoretical aspects of bosonic quantum computing. Requirements We are looking for an excellent scientist with expertise in quantum computing and quantum information processing in general, with a strong interest in bosonic quantum computing and/or characterisation or testing/learning theory. Needed qualifications for candidates include proven research talent and good academic writing and presentation skills. Candidates are expected to have an excellent command of English. Terms and conditions The terms of employment are in accordance with the Dutch Collective Labour Agreement for Research Centres ("CAO-onderzoeksinstellingen"). The gross monthly salary for an employee on a full time basis, depending on relevant work experience, ranges from € 4,374 to € 5,758. The appointment will be for a period of one year, with the option to extend 1.5 more years (for a total of 2.5) by mutual agreement. Employees are also entitled to a holiday allowance of 8% of the gross annual salary ...
